newsitem.title: UK: Italy's Bertinotti against public spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bertinotti against public spending cuts.

text.p: Fausto Bertinotti, leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which ensures the government a parliamentary majority, on Friday said he was opposed to further cuts in public spending in the 1998 budget.
"We are very much opposed to the idea of spending cuts," Bertinotti told a meeting of bankers and financiers in London.
Bertinotti said public spending in Italy was below that of a number of its European partners while tax evasion in the country remained at unacceptable levels.
"I don't see any reason why we should cut spending in Italy."
Bertinotti is a key player in Italy's debate over welfare reform, seen as vital if Italy is to make the first round of entrants into Europe's single currency.
